messages:
elaine: heads up — seeing persistent latency spikes on edge-gpu nodes in apac-edge-3, looks like some tenants are routing through an extra hop and blowing egress queues :confused:
raj: :eyes: can you paste the traceroute and an exabgp dump if you have one?
elaine: traceroute output: `traceroute to 10.11.8.4 (10.11.8.4), 8 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1 10.11.0.1 0.45 ms 0.33 ms 0.29 ms
 2 10.11.1.5 1.23 ms 1.10 ms 1.15 ms
 3 192.168.254.6 12.1 ms 12.0 ms 12.2 ms
 4 172.30.5.2 45.8 ms 46.1 ms 46.0 ms
 5 10.11.8.4 46.2 ms 46.0 ms 45.9 ms`
elaine: and the noisy tenant is tenant-id: t-92f3, high tail latency for tail-50/95/99, token-per-second pattern looks bursty
marta: infra-bot alerted this morning too: `infra-bot: apac-edge-3 egress queue depth > 70% for 12m, affected nodes: edge-gpu-07..edge-gpu-09`
raj: hmm extra hop at step 3/4 — could be a regional peering change or a routing loop to transit. Did we recently push the AS-path rewrite in the edge fabric?
elaine: pushed small BGP tweak yesterday to steer some traffic to a new transit to save cost. rollback would hit us $$ but we can fail traffic to dedicated pools if needed.
tom: cost vs stability tradeoff — if t-92f3 is bucket-heavy, isolating to dedicated-slice for 24h might be cheaper than rollback and risk across tenants.
marta: can we pin just that tenant to the apac-dedicated-pool-2 via routing-policy: `route-map TENANT_T92F3 permit 10; set next-hop add 10.12.0.2` ?
raj: yeah but that will increase prefill/warmup cost on that pool. Estimate: +12 GPU-hours and 0.6% of pool capacity for the day.
elaine: provisional mitigation plan: 1) re-route t-92f3 to dedicated pool 2) throttle egress for noisy tenant at proxy layer 3) monitor queue depth and latency for 2h then decide rollback of BGP tweak if still bad
elaine: anyone have the curl to hit the router policy API? I can do the carve now.
raj: `POST /api/v1/routing/tenants/t-92f3/steer` payload: `{\"target_pool\":\"apac-dedicated-pool-2\",\"ttl_hours\":24}` — need auth scope `routing:modify`
marta: i pushed the steer, infra-bot reports: `infra-bot: routing change applied for t-92f3 -> apac-dedicated-pool-2, change_id c-8839`
elaine: thank you — starting telemetry collection.
infra-bot: infra-bot: metric snapshot: egress_queue_depth (apac-edge-3) before=76% after=42% (1m after steer)
elaine: nice drop :tada: tail latency 99 went from 820ms -> 210ms on affected nodes (first 10m window)
tom: good improvement. keep an eye on cross-pool saturation — we don't want to move noisy tenancy to a dedicated pool and starve other reserved customers.
raj: agreed — let's add temporary soft cap on t-92f3 to 200 RPS and enable prefix KV-cache eviction to reduce long KV traces that hog memory on those VMs
marta: added proxy throttle: `tenant_throttle.set('t-92f3', rps=200, burst=50)` and enabled `kvcache.eviction_policy=LRU_threshold_0.8` for that pool
elaine: telemetry after 40m: egress_queue_depth steady ~38%, KV cache miss rate down 15%, tail p99 ~180ms. Looks good.
tom: can we quantify expected cost impact for tomorrow if tenant keeps this profile? we should propose either enforced dedicated carve or recommend a pricing adjustment.
raj: rough calc: today steering cost + prefill = ~14 GPU-hours @ spot avg => $X (internal calc), plus expected 25% higher egress from dedicated network. I'll run a precise report and post in the morning.
elaine: ops note: keep steer until 2025-07-03 06:00 UTC, then auto-unsteer unless infra team approves extension.
marta: added alert: `if egress_queue_depth > 60% OR p99 > 400ms -> auto-unsteer and notify #oncall`
elaine: question — should we consider route-change rollbacks as last resort only? this BGP tweak saved money on low-traffic days but it made edge hop-count sensitive to bursty tenants
tom: yes rollback is last resort. We need a playbook: 1) isolate noisy tenant to dedicated 2) proxy-throttle 3) capacity scale dedicated pool 4) rollback BGP only if systemic
raj: filing follow-up item: open ticket INFRA-1182 "assess AS-path steering risk for apac-edge" and include cost vs p99 curves, assign to me
elaine: thanks all. leaving monitoring on — ping me if anything regresses :wave:
